qa.recommendation: GEM shows 131.6 MW, which is seven engines at 18.8 MW from the EIA-860M table. The sources give different numbers. Please decide whether to keep the EIA figure.
qa.note: The Burns and McDonnell press release (https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/burns--mcdonnell-reaches-substantial-completion-on-aj-mihm-and-fd-kuester-reciprocating-engine-power-generating-stations-in-michigans-upper-peninsula-300838584.html) gives 126 MW for the station, at about 18 MW per engine. The Michigan air permit staff report from January 2026 (https://mienviro.michigan.gov/ncore/downloadpdf/-7185968111409593870) says each engine drives a 19,260 kW generator, which would be 134.8 MW for seven. The Public Service Commission cases U-21081 and U-21542 give 125.6 MW. The EIA-860M table for September 2026 (https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx) gives 18.8 MW per engine, so 131.6 MW. I did not change the value because the sources disagree and none is clearly the nameplate rating.
